//: Mutation matrix for the CUE SHEET PARSER (issue #196, part 3). Half of these break the MM:SS:FF arithmetic in one of the ways it is broken in the wild — FF as hundredths, FF as milliseconds, truncation instead of rounding, a frame count of 75 accepted — and every one of them produces a playable album whose tracks all start slightly off, with nothing erroring and nothing logged. That is precisely why they are here: the only thing standing between this feature and a silently wrong track list is an assertion on a literal. The rest break the decisions the parser owns: which INDEX is the boundary, when a sheet must be refused, when a cue changes nothing at all, and the two things about mpv's EDL syntax that make a clip url loadable. Driven by native/tools/mutate.py (never a hand-rolled loop; see CONTRIBUTING).

mutants.//: THE BUG THIS FEATURE IS MOST LIKELY TO SHIP WITH. FF read as hundredths of a second: every track after the first starts up to a second early, the album plays, nothing complains.
mutants.name: frames-are-hundredths

mutants.//: FF read as milliseconds — the other wrong reading, and the one that looks most like the code is doing nothing.
mutants.name: frames-are-milliseconds

mutants.//: A CD second holds frames 0..74. Accepting 75+ turns a broken sheet into a plausible one placed a fraction of a second out.
mutants.name: frame-75-accepted
mutants.find: if (ff >= kFramesPerSecond) return 0;     // a second holds frames 0..74 — see the header
mutants.replace: if (ff >= 1000) return 0;                 // a second holds frames 0..74 — see the header

mutants.name: sixty-second-minute-accepted
mutants.find: if (ss > 59) return 0;                    // a minute holds 60 seconds; a sheet saying otherwise is broken
mutants.replace: if (ss > 5900) return 0;                  // a minute holds 60 seconds; a sheet saying otherwise is broken

mutants.//: THE BOUNDARY. Ending a track at the NEXT track's pregap instead of its INDEX 01 moves every boundary on the album by however long the run-in is, and disagrees with mpv's own cue demuxer about the same file.
mutants.name: pregap-moves-the-boundary

mutants.//: The other half of the same rule, from the parser's side: an INDEX 00 that wins over the INDEX 01 written after it.
mutants.name: pregap-wins-over-index-01

mutants.//: REFUSAL. isValid's starting value is what catches a track nothing could place: an unplaced track is -1, and `prev` starts at -1 so the very first one fails the same comparison a backwards one does. Move that starting value and the sheet becomes valid with a segment beginning at millisecond -1.
mutants.name: unplaceable-track-accepted
mutants.find:
int prev = -1;
        for (const Track& t : f.tracks)
mutants.replace:
int prev = -2;
        for (const Track& t : f.tracks)

mutants.name: zero-length-track-accepted
mutants.find:
if (t.startMs <= prev) return false;
            prev = t.startMs;
mutants.replace:
if (t.startMs < prev) return false;
            prev = t.startMs;

mutants.//: 'THIS CUE CHANGES NOTHING' is one function's answer. Expanding the first FILE of a multi-FILE sheet silently drops every other disc.
mutants.name: multi-file-sheet-expanded
mutants.find: if (sheet.files.size() != 1) return out;   // a cue over per-track files: that album is already correct
mutants.replace: if (sheet.files.isEmpty()) return out;     // a cue over per-track files: that album is already correct

mutants.//: The performer fallback lives in ONE place so no caller repeats it; drop it and every track of a normally-tagged sheet loses its artist.
mutants.name: no-performer-fallback

mutants.//: THE LAST TRACK'S FAKED LENGTH. mpv reports whatever length an EDL entry claims as the DURATION, so a zero here makes the closing song show as zero seconds long and a too-large one makes the progress bar lie for its whole duration.
mutants.name: last-track-gets-a-length
mutants.find:
if (endMs > start)
        url += QLatin1Char(',') + QString::number((endMs - start) / 1000.0, 'f', 3);
mutants.replace: url += QLatin1Char(',') + QString::number(((endMs > start ? endMs : start) - start) / 1000.0, 'f', 3);

mutants.//: mpv's EDL counts BYTES. Using QChars truncates the filename by one per non-ASCII character, and the album simply fails to load.
mutants.name: clip-url-counts-characters

mutants.//: Drop the length prefix altogether and every path with a comma in it splits into three EDL fields.
mutants.name: clip-url-unquoted
mutants.find: QString url = QStringLiteral("edl://%") + QString::number(bytes) + QLatin1Char('%') + filePath

mutants.//: ENCODINGS. Skipping the strict-UTF-8 attempt reads every modern sheet as Latin-1, which is mojibake in every accented name.
mutants.name: utf8-never-tried

mutants.//: …and the other way: no Latin-1 fallback, so a Windows-1252 sheet decodes to replacement characters.
mutants.name: no-latin1-fallback

mutants.//: A mixed-mode disc's data track is a filesystem. Expanding it adds a track that plays nothing and shifts every number after it.
mutants.name: data-tracks-are-music

mutants.//: FILE lines: dropping the trailing format word unconditionally renames a file genuinely called 'Live WAVE.flac'.
mutants.name: format-word-always-dropped

mutants.//: Which file a sheet is about. Requiring the extension to match too refuses the majority of real single-file rips, whose sheet still names the .wav they were transcoded from.
mutants.name: extension-must-match

mutants.//: …and the opposite: matching on the base name of anything at all would let one folder's sheet claim a neighbour it was never about.
mutants.name: any-file-matches
